description: Machine-readable representation of UK Universal Credit eligibility criteria

check_age_eligibility.routing_logic: Under 16: not eligible. Age 16-17: check special circumstances. Age 18 to State Pension age: check basic eligibility. State Pension age or over: not eligible.

check_youth_eligibility.question: Does the 16-17 year old meet any special circumstances for eligibility?
check_youth_eligibility.help_text: 16-17 year olds can only claim Universal Credit under specific circumstances
check_youth_eligibility.evaluation_logic: If ANY path is satisfied, proceed to UK residency check. If NONE are met, ineligible due to age.

paths.description: Has health condition or disability with medical evidence
paths.requirement: Has health condition or disability with medical evidence (fit note)

paths.description: Caring for someone receiving health/disability benefit
paths.requirement: Caring for someone who receives a health or disability benefit

paths.description: Lives with partner, responsible for child, partner eligible
criteria: Partner is eligible for Universal Credit

paths.description: Pregnant with baby due in next 11 weeks
paths.requirement: Pregnant and baby is due in the next 11 weeks
Had a baby in the last 15 weeks

check_partner_under_pension_age.question: Do you live with a partner who is under State Pension age?
check_partner_under_pension_age.help_text: If one partner has reached State Pension age but the other hasn't, you can still claim Universal Credit together until both reach pension age

check_uk_residency.question: Do you live in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?
check_uk_residency.help_text: You must be living in the UK to claim Universal Credit. Armed forces personnel stationed abroad can apply using a specific address.

check_eu_eea_swiss_status.question: If you are an EU, EEA, or Swiss citizen, do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
check_eu_eea_swiss_status.help_text: UK citizens and those with settled/pre-settled status can proceed. Not applicable if you are not an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen.

check_capital_limit.question: Do you (and your partner if claiming jointly) have £16,000 or less in total savings, capital, and investments?
check_capital_limit.help_text: Savings includes cash, bank accounts, ISAs, Premium Bonds, stocks, shares, cryptoassets, property you don't live in, and certain other capital. Your main home and personal possessions don't count.

criteria.calculation_method: If capital is £16,001 or more: not eligible. If capital is £6,001-£16,000: payment reduced by £4.35 per month for every £250 (or part thereof) above £6,000. If capital is £6,000 or less: no reduction.
capital_includes: Cash and bank accounts (including PayPal, digital-only accounts)
Savings accounts (bank, building society, credit union)
ISAs (cash, stocks and shares, Lifetime ISAs)
Property you own but don't live in (with exceptions)
Unspent income from previous assessment periods
capital_excludes: Property you own and live in (main residence)
Life insurance policies not yet paid out
Business accounts for active businesses or those closed within 6 months
Property that is the main home of close relatives who are retired or have severe health condition
Property that is the main home of former partner who is a lone parent

check_student_status.description: Determine if student status affects eligibility
check_student_status.routing_logic: If not a student or studying part-time and available for work: eligible. If studying full-time: check for student eligibility exceptions.

check_student_eligibility_exceptions.question: As a full-time student, do you meet any of the eligibility exceptions?
check_student_eligibility_exceptions.help_text: Full-time students are generally not eligible for Universal Credit unless they meet specific circumstances
check_student_eligibility_exceptions.evaluation_logic: If ANY path is satisfied, proceed to joint claim check. If NONE are met, ineligible as full-time student.

paths.description: Age 21 or under in full-time non-advanced education without parental support
criteria: Studying full-time non-advanced education (A-levels, T-levels, NVQ Level 3 or below)

paths.description: Responsible for a child (adopted or foster)
paths.requirement: Responsible for a child (adopted child or foster child)

paths.description: Lives with partner who is eligible for Universal Credit
paths.requirement: Lives with a partner who is eligible for Universal Credit

paths.description: Reached State Pension age and lives with partner below that age
paths.requirement: Reached State Pension age and lives with a partner who is below State Pension age
Received a Migration Notice letter requiring move to Universal Credit

paths.description: Disabled with limited capability for work and receiving qualifying benefit
criteria: Assessed as having limited capability for work BEFORE starting the course

Receiving one of: Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Disability Living Allowance (DLA), Attendance Allowance, Armed Forces Independence Payment, Adult Disability Payment (ADP) in Scotland, Child Disability Payment (CDP) in Scotland, Pension Age Disability Payment (PADP) in Scotland, Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance (SADLA)

paths.description: Studying full-time non-advanced education with no student loan/grant and available for work
criteria: No student loan or maintenance grant
From 1 September after 19th birthday if course is more than 12 hours per week

check_joint_claim_requirement.question: If you live with a partner, are you making a joint claim together?
check_joint_claim_requirement.help_text: Couples living together must make a joint claim for Universal Credit, even if only one partner is eligible. Both partners' income and savings are combined for assessment.

ELIGIBLE.description: You meet the basic eligibility criteria for Universal Credit
next_steps: You'll need: email address, bank account details, housing details (rent/mortgage), childcare costs if applicable
If you have capital between £6,000-£16,000, your payment will be reduced by £4.35 per month for every £250 (or part thereof) above £6,000
You may be eligible for additional payments if you have a health condition, disability, caring responsibilities, or children
Await your first payment (usually 5 weeks after application)
You may be able to request an advance payment if in financial hardship

INELIGIBLE_too_young.guidance: Universal Credit is not available for people under 16. Your parent or guardian may be able to claim Universal Credit which includes an amount for you as a dependent child.

INELIGIBLE_age_16_17_no_circumstances.guidance: 16-17 year olds can only claim Universal Credit if they: have a health condition/disability with medical evidence, are caring for someone receiving health/disability benefit, are nearing end of life, are responsible for a child, live with eligible partner and responsible for child, are pregnant (baby due in 11 weeks), had baby in last 15 weeks, or have no parental support. If none apply, you may be eligible for other benefits. Check www.gov.uk/benefits-calculators

INELIGIBLE_pension_age.reason: At or above State Pension age without eligible partner under pension age
INELIGIBLE_pension_age.guidance: Universal Credit is not available once you reach State Pension age (unless your partner is under State Pension age). You may be eligible for Pension Credit instead. Check www.gov.uk/pension-credit

INELIGIBLE_not_uk_resident.guidance: You must live in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland) to claim Universal Credit. If you are in the armed forces and stationed abroad, you may still be able to apply using a specific address. Contact your unit's welfare officer for guidance.

INELIGIBLE_no_settled_status.reason: EU, EEA, or Swiss citizen without settled or pre-settled status
INELIGIBLE_no_settled_status.guidance: EU, EEA, and Swiss citizens generally need settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme to claim Universal Credit. Apply for settled status at www.gov.uk/settled-status-eu-citizens-families. If you arrived in the UK after 31 December 2020, different immigration rules may apply.

INELIGIBLE_capital_over_16000.reason: Total capital, savings, and investments exceed £16,000
INELIGIBLE_capital_over_16000.guidance: You are not eligible for Universal Credit if you (and your partner if claiming jointly) have more than £16,000 in total capital, savings, and investments. This includes: cash, bank accounts, ISAs, Premium Bonds, stocks, shares, cryptoassets, and property you don't live in (with some exceptions). Your main home and personal possessions don't count. If your capital reduces to £16,000 or below in the future, you can reapply. See www.gov.uk/guidance/universal-credit-money-savings-and-investments for full details of what counts.

INELIGIBLE_full_time_student.guidance: Full-time students are generally not eligible for Universal Credit unless they: are aged 21 or under in non-advanced education without parental support, are responsible for a child, live with an eligible partner, have reached State Pension age with younger partner, received a Migration Notice, are disabled with limited capability for work and receiving qualifying disability benefits, or are in non-advanced education with no student loan/grant and available for work. If none apply, you may be able to claim Student Finance. Part-time students who are available for work can claim Universal Credit. See www.gov.uk/guidance/universal-credit-and-students

INELIGIBLE_must_claim_jointly.reason: Living with partner but not making a joint claim
INELIGIBLE_must_claim_jointly.guidance: If you live with a partner, you must make a joint claim for Universal Credit together. You cannot make separate claims. Both partners' income and savings will be combined and assessed together, even if only one of you is working or eligible. To proceed, you need to apply jointly at www.gov.uk/apply-universal-credit

age_limits.maximum_age_description: Under State Pension age (varies by date of birth)
age_limits.note: State Pension age varies - check www.gov.uk/state-pension-age

capital_limits.calculation_note: For every £250 (or part thereof) between £6,000 and £16,000, Universal Credit is reduced by £4.35 per month

qualifying_disability_benefits: Pension Age Disability Payment (PADP) in Scotland

assessment_period.note: Universal Credit is paid monthly based on your circumstances in each assessment period

capital_calculation.rule: Capital between £6,000-£16,000 generates tariff income that reduces Universal Credit payment

examples.explanation: £300 above threshold, treated as 2 complete bands of £250
At maximum capital limit, £10,000 above threshold

capital_calculation.note: Any remaining amount that is not a complete £250 counts as another full band (always round up)

joint_claim.rule: Couples living together must make a joint claim
joint_claim.assessment: Both partners' income and savings are combined
joint_claim.exception: No exceptions - even if one partner is not eligible, must claim jointly
joint_claim.consequence: Separate claims by partners living together will be rejected

student_eligibility.general_rule: Full-time students are not eligible unless they meet specific exceptions
student_eligibility.part_time_rule: Part-time students can claim if available for work
student_eligibility.student_income: Student loans and maintenance grants are counted as income, with £110 per assessment period disregarded for full-time students
student_eligibility.non_advanced_education_threshold: From 1 September after 19th birthday, if course is more than 12 hours per week and no student loan/grant available
student_eligibility.limited_capability_for_work: Must be assessed BEFORE starting course to qualify as disabled student
student_eligibility.qualifying_benefits_required: Disabled students must receive one of the qualifying disability benefits listed in constants

age_16_17_eligibility.rule: 16-17 year olds can only claim under specific circumstances
circumstances: Health condition/disability with medical evidence (fit note)
Caring for someone receiving health/disability benefit
Live with partner who is eligible and responsible for child
Pregnant with baby due in next 11 weeks
No parental support (not living with parents, not in local authority care)
age_16_17_eligibility.assessment: Any ONE of these circumstances is sufficient for eligibility

pension_age_transition.rule: Universal Credit stops when both partners reach State Pension age
pension_age_transition.mixed_age_couple: If one partner has reached State Pension age but the other hasn't, can still claim Universal Credit together
pension_age_transition.transition: When second partner reaches State Pension age, Universal Credit ends and couple should claim Pension Credit
